proposals: Grid Controller of India, as CCTS registry, should publish monthly figures for Carbon Credit Certificates issued, transferred, surrendered and banked, by sector and vintage, so the oversupply risk IEEFA attaches to unlimited banking can be watched in the data rather than argued in the abstract.

CERC should write into its Carbon Credit Certificate regulations a dated review of the no-expiry banking rule, to be decided on published registry data on banked surpluses against compliance demand, so the choice between keeping and adding an expiry is made on evidence.

CERC should publish the actual floor and forbearance price values and a fixed date for the first CCC trading session on the approved power exchanges, so obligated entities and lenders are not relying on reported expectations of an October 2026 start.

The Bureau of Energy Efficiency should publish a mapping of each of its 12 offset methodologies against the ICVCM Core Carbon Principles, so whether CCTS offset credits meet the benchmark international lenders use is stated by the administrator rather than left as an open question.

The Bureau of Energy Efficiency should publish its accreditation procedure for offset verifiers, stating whether bodies already accredited under the CDM will be recognised, so project developers know which validators they may use before investing in an offset project.
